sections.html:
Newton sits in Middlesex County roughly 8 miles from downtown Boston, and it has no single downtown. Thirteen villages make up the city, and people use the village name when they give an address: Auburndale, Chestnut Hill, Newton Centre, Newton Corner, Newton Highlands, Newtonville, Nonantum, Oak Hill, Waban and West Newton, along with Newton Lower Falls, Newton Upper Falls and Thompsonville.

The land area is 18.16 square miles. Newton had 88,923 residents in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 90,741. Villages have no legal borders, so the name on a listing or deed can differ from what a neighbor's mail says. Eleven ZIP codes cover the city, 02458 through 02468, with 02495 used for Nonantum. Check your parcel details with the assessor before you list. Buyers shopping in one village often compare it with the next one over, so a clear description of where your house sits helps.

Newton's character is residential and varied. Some villages grew around old mill sites on the Charles River, while others were built out as streetcar and commuter neighborhoods, so house ages and conditions run across a wide range even on neighboring streets.

Property classFY2026 certified rate
Residential$9.69 per $1,000

Two city offices split the work. Assessing determines what your house is worth on paper and rules on abatements, exemptions and excise adjustments. Treasury and Collector sends the bills and takes payment.

FY2027 exemption applications are due on or before April 1, 2027. If you plan to hold the house through the winter before you sell, put that date on your calendar.

Visit Newton City Hall, 1000 Commonwealth Avenue in Newton Centre, and ask for Room 111. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and you can phone 617-796-1160.

Exemption, deferral and work-off programs are available to eligible owners. The Newton assessing page hosts the assessor's database and the application forms. Look up your own parcel before you speak with a buyer, because the database shows what the city has on file for your house.

Newton grew up around seven hills: Nonantum, Waban, Chestnut Hill, Bald Pate, Oak Hill, Institution Hill and Mount Ida. Because the ground rises and falls from one village to the next, drainage, basements and the way a house sits on its lot are not the same everywhere. The Charles River borders the north and west of the city, and Crystal Lake, a 33-acre natural lake, lies in Newton Centre.

About 53.6 inches of precipitation fall in a typical year, and winters are cold, which is hard on roofs, chimneys, gutters and foundations. Near the river or the lake, an inspector may press on moisture and drainage. On a slope, grading is the usual question. If you know your basement has taken on water, say so to your attorney before you sign a purchase agreement.

Newton has MBTA light rail, commuter rail and bus service, and the Mass Pike crosses the northern part of town. Route 128 touches the western edge.

  • The Green Line D branch, known as the Riverside branch, goes through the middle of the city and ends at Newton Lower Falls. Riders reach downtown Boston in 10 to 30 minutes.
  • The B branch stops across from Boston College on Commonwealth Avenue.
  • Commuter rail on the Worcester line serves the northern villages near Waltham.
  • Express buses use the Mass Pike to reach downtown Boston.
  • Routes 9, 30 and 16 run east to west. Nearly every north-south street ends inside the city, so Newton has no major north-south road.

The Newtonville commuter rail station is scheduled to close in December 2026 for accessibility work and reopen in spring 2029. A house close to that station may get questions from commuters.

A typical Newton sale involves a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate issued by the fire department, clear title and nearly always an attorney.

  • Set the alarm inspection as soon as a closing date exists. What the inspector checks depends on when the house was built and when its last permit was issued.
  • Replace any battery alarm that is expired or lacks a date with a sealed 10-year photoelectric model with a hush feature.
  • Your deed is recorded at the county registry of deeds. The Secretary of the Commonwealth runs an email alert that tells you when a new document is recorded against your property.
  • The deeds excise follows Chapter 64D, Section 1 and is figured per $500 of price.

Land Court registered land is rarer than recorded land in Massachusetts. Your attorney will tell you which type your lot is.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you call
sections.html:
Preparation shortens the timeline. Pull together your deed, the latest tax bill, permit records for any work done on the house and any notes about water in the basement. For an estate, add the court or estate paperwork, because heirs have to show authority before a deed can pass to a buyer.

Ask the Assessing Department whether an exemption or deferral on your bill ends when the property changes hands. Your attorney will also need payoff figures for any mortgage or unpaid tax balance. When these documents sit in one folder, the attorney reviews them once instead of chasing pieces over several weeks.

A short sequence works for most owners. Start with the tax bill and the assessor record. Book the alarm inspection once a date is set. Hand everything to the attorney, then compare the offer with the dates and repairs a regular listing would involve. Nobody can make you take an offer, and you can ask for a different closing date.

Plenty of Newton owners hold a house that needs updating, or they are settling an estate or moving on short notice. A mortgage buyer's inspection can turn up alarm upgrades and repair items on an older house, and sellers often reach for a cash sale to avoid that round of negotiation.

A cash buyer removes lender approval from the schedule. The fire certificate, title work and recording happen regardless, and a tax balance has to be cleared before the deed goes over. Cash Home Buyers can look at a Newton house as it stands and you owe nothing if you decline. Set the offer next to what a listing would involve in repairs, showings and time, and pick the route that suits you. If a relocation or an estate sets the deadline, tell the buyer early so the closing date can be planned around it from the start.

faqs.q: How many villages are in Newton, MA?
faqs.a: Newton has thirteen villages: Auburndale, Chestnut Hill, Newton Centre, Newton Corner, Newton Highlands, Newton Lower Falls, Newton Upper Falls, Newtonville, Nonantum, Oak Hill, Thompsonville, Waban and West Newton.

faqs.q: What is the Newton residential property tax rate?
faqs.a: The certified FY2026 residential rate is $9.69 per $1,000 of assessed value. Commercial, industrial and personal property is taxed at $18.06.

faqs.q: Does Newton have a Green Line stop?
faqs.a: Yes. The D branch crosses the middle of the city to Newton Lower Falls, and the B branch ends at Boston College on the Brighton line.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Newton?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires one from the local fire department whenever a home is sold or transferred. The department charges a fee, so call to book the visit.

faqs.q: When is the Newton exemption application deadline?
faqs.a: Applications for FY2027 exemptions and tax assistance are due on or before April 1, 2027. Call the assessing office to confirm which forms apply to you.
